President Donald Trump is once again comparing himself to legendary figures, this time the Greek mythological character Atlas.

On Saturday, Trump posted what appears to be an AI-generated image depicting himself literally holding the world on his shoulders. He is on one knee and is draped in an American flag.

The image appears to be a reference to Atlas, the Titan from Greek mythology tasked with holding the celestial spheres on his shoulders. Later depictions — and those most people are familiar with — depict him holding the Earth.

Presumably, Trump's intention here is to suggest he, like Atlas, must take on the burden of supporting the entire world on his own. In Greek myth, Atlas's eternal labor was actually a punishment for joining with other Titans in rebellion against the Olympian gods.

The post had no caption, so it's unclear what he meant to communicate with the image. The post was made a day after U.S. forces launched an attack against drone storage sites in Iran. The attack appears to be a retaliatory act following an attack on a commercial shipping vessel that was moving through the Strait of Hormuz.

President Donald Trump posted what appears to be an AI-generated image of himself holding up the world like the Greek mythological figure Atlas ( Truth Social )

Trump also posted an image on Saturday comparing himself at age 20 to former President Barack Obama at age 18. The photo he chose of himself shows him in 1964 in a military-style uniform while he attended the New York Military Academy.

The photo he chose of Obama showed the former president with a marijuana joint in his mouth. The photo was taken during his time at Occidental College.

The Independent has requested comment from the White House.

It's not the first time Trump has posted an image seemingly comparing himself to a god-like figure. Earlier this year, he had to explain why he posted an image on Truth Social that appeared to depict him as Jesus healing a sick man.

The bizarre image featured Trump in a white clerical robe with a red priest's stole draped around his neck. Light is emanating from his hands and he is reaching down with his right hand to presumably heal or bless a sick man in a hospital bed. A nurse, a woman, a veteran and a U.S. service member stare on in awe. A group of what appear to be U.S. soldiers — including one that looks like they're wearing a mech suit — are floating over his head in the sun. Three jets race overhead, including two that look as though they're about to collide.

The AI-generated image enraged even some Republicans, who saw it as sacrilege for the president to so directly compare himself to Jesus.

"This goes too far. It crosses the line," David Brody, a journalist with the Christian Broadcasting Network, wrote at the time. "A supporter can back the mission and reject this."

After deleting the image, Trump was asked what it was meant to convey, and insisted he never intended to compare himself with Jesus, instead saying he thought the picture was showing him as a doctor.

"It's supposed to be as a doctor making people better," he said at the time. "And I do make people better. I make people a lot better."

He explained why he deleted the image to CBS News, saying he "didn't want to have anybody be confused" by the image.

"People were confused," he said.

Shoaib Bashir backed England not to crack in their third Test decider against New Zealand but admitted the Trent Bridge pitch had already started to do so.

After two days of glorious batting conditions in the winner takes all clash in Nottingham, the bowlers finally got some payback as 11 wickets fell on a surface that had started to open up under the summer sun.

England lost eight for 130 to hand the Black Caps an 84-run first-innings lead, then shot back with three quick breakthroughs before Rachin Ravindra took control.

His 60 not out put New Zealand 204 in front at the end of the third evening, with seven wickets in hand as they attempt to leave a chase that kills off English hopes of victory.

And Bashir, who found some useful turn but failed to take a wicket in nine overs before stumps, did not shy away from how difficult batting last is likely to be.

“Obviously the wicket is deteriorating. The way it played today, it had a bit in it,” said the spinner, who was wary of speculating on what his side might be able to hunt down.

“I wouldn’t want to put a number on it, especially with this England side because we’ve got some unbelievable cricketers in this team, but as little as possible with the way it’s deteriorating. The wicket played around a bit and we’ve got to find a way to counteract that.

open image in gallery It was a challenging day for England captain Ben Stokes, left, and Shoaib Bashir, right (Mike Egerton/PA) ( PA Wire )

“The series is on the line, we’re going to try and win. I’m human, we are going to feel the pressure, but there’s a lot of excitement going into the next two days too.”

New Zealand seamer Zak Foulkes, who entered the game as a concussion substitute for Blair Tickner, claimed two huge wickets when he clean bowled Ben Stokes and Harry Brook. He suggested the wearing surface had given him a boost on both occasions and was crossing his fingers for more of the same.

“I’m going to say they hit cracks, which is a good sign with us bowling last,” he said.

open image in gallery Harry Brook was bowled by this Zak Foulkes delivery (Mike Egerton/PA) ( PA Wire )

“We just had to probe away at the top of off (stump) and the odd one would do something to give us a reward.

“English conditions aren’t really used to this hot heat so it’s prone to cracking. I think the groundsmen were worried about the dryness of the surface before the Test with the weather we had leading up to this, but I think the next couple of days could be pretty enjoyable.

“That’s the beauty of bowling last. Hopefully the wicket is going to be at its hardest for batting right at the end and we can make use of it.”

News.title: How stubborn Marcelo Bielsa provoked the bitter demise of Uruguay in World Cup implosion
News.content:

For five minutes, Luis Suarez sat down opposite Marcelo Bielsa and explained his frustrations with how things were in the Uruguay camp.

The Uruguayans were in the USA for Copa America 2024 and a group that had become accustomed to being able to do things a certain way under previous regimes were bristling at seemingly needless restrictions being put into place by Bielsa, their coach who is as famous for his genius as his idiosyncrasies.

In truth, the grievances seem pretty minor.

"At the Celeste Complex, employees are not allowed to come in and greet us and eat with us," he said.

"They have to be careful even at the door they have to enter. It breaks my heart that this is how life is in the Complex today.”

On a similar track, in New York, Bielsa had asked the players not to go out and greet fans only for Suarez to stand up and tell him they were going to do it anyway. It kept adding on to an existing tension between the most senior player in the squad and the man charged with leading them to glory.

Once Suarez had completed what, in his own recollection, was five uninterrupted minutes of speaking, he paused, awaiting a response from his coach.

open image in gallery Uruguay have been eliminated after a disastrous World Cup 2026 ( Getty )

“Thank you very much,” Bielsa said.

And that was that. Within weeks, Uruguay were out after losing the semi-final to Colombia and Suarez had retired from international football, Bielsa’s curt response the final insult, and Suarez went on a media tour to let everybody know how he felt. That began a mediatic war in this tiny, football-obsessed country from which the current iteration of Uruguay never recovered.

Before the rupture with Suarez, Uruguay had won 11 and drawn five of their 18 games under Bielsa, including notable wins over Brazil and Argentina.

After it, there were just five wins in 17 games, including a 5-1 humbling by the United States and a winless World Cup 2026 campaign, something thought impossible when the two-time champions were drawn in a group with Saudi Arabia and Cape Verde. The team lost its temper, their coach did too, and it’s the end of their story together. The Uruguayan FA has even reportedly cancelled a chartered return flight, with players forced to return on commercial flights.

open image in gallery Uruguay's Agustin Canobbio is shown a red card by referee Ismail Elfath ( Reuters )

Bielsa is, in many ways, the complete opposite to his Conmebol contemporary Carlo Ancelotti. Ancelotti has never been considered a tactical mastermind, but is one of the best ever at managing the vibes, keeping players engaged and striking the right balance of freedom and instruction. Bielsa is an unavoidably awkward man, who can speak in long, rambling screeds or puncture you with short shrift but a tactical mind, praised by Pep Guardiola as a “genius,” who is obsessed with the minutiae and details of coaching.

What is notable about the contrasts in the two coaches for this tournament was that Ancelotti called up Neymar Jr. beforehand and told him that as long as he didn’t mind being a substitute that he wanted him in the squad. Ancelotti knew it was better to have Neymar on the inside than the outside, particularly if results wobbled, and managed it deftly. Suarez swallowed his pride in May and approached Bielsa about returning for one Last Dance. The Argentine coach gave him a one word answer, and it wasn’t yes.

open image in gallery Uruguay coach Marcelo Bielsa speaks to the media after the match ( Reuters )

Nahitan Nandez, a Suarez ally, was also left out and his omission was such a surprise that Bielsa had to come out and clarify that it was for “footballing reasons only”. Matias Vecino had been jettisoned in 2024, but quieter Suarez allies were still included. Uruguay didn’t have enough talent to leave them out, but it meant the camp was split before they arrived at their tournament training base in Cancun. This morning they were cleaning that base out.

To say that the Suarez fallout was the turning point of this reign would be an understatement. And it may prove to be the end of a famous coaching career.

Over decades of managing football teams in his idiosyncratic style, Bielsa has amassed something of a cult following.

When the players buy in, they truly buy in. Think of Chile’s success, knocking out world champions Spain at the 2014 World Cup playing scintillating football, or Leeds United, where he held the city in the palm of his hand after returning them to the Premier League. He is so revered at Newell’s Old Boys that their stadium is named after him, not something that tends to happen to people while they’re still living, let alone coaching.

open image in gallery Spain's Alex Baena scores their first goal past Uruguay's Fernando Muslera ( Reuters )

There have also been famous blow-ups.

At Lazio, his reign can be counted in days rather than months. In Lille you could count it in months but you’d only need one hand. At Marseille he resigned after losing the first game of his second season.

Now, if you’ve ever been in a room with Marcelo Bielsa then you’ll know he’s not exactly brimming with traditional charisma. The way that the Argentine has won over players and united teams in the past is through his work, rather than his glittering personality.

In the wake of the Suarez rupture, the squad never felt fully united or even uniteable, if that is even a word. A coach who, more than most, needs absolute buy-in was dealing with a split squad that had been destabilised to the point of dysfunction and seeded with doubts.

The famous Uruguayan spirit, la garra charrúa, is a never-say-die attitude named for the natives who lived on the pampas long before Europeans arrived, and represents those typical battling qualities you would associate with their teams of the past. Not so much the one we’ve seen over the past two weeks.

As a country with a small population, talent development is always going to be a puzzle for the AUF. The domestic league is tiny, dominated financially by two giants from the capital, and so much of the best talent leaves in its teenage years to develop in their bigger neighbours or further afield — a similar set-up to somewhere like Ireland.

open image in gallery Uruguay's Darwin Nunez reacts against Spain ( Reuters )

Their success over recent decades has come from building a tough-tackling, rock-solid team in defence and midfield, infused with that garra charrúa, while affording freedom to a generation of elite attacking players.

Diego Forlan propelled them to success in 2010, Edinson Cavani and Luis Suarez then followed. With a solid base, that stellar attacking talent (all of whom are still relentless harriers out of possession) made Uruguay a frightening opponent. Now, their elite talent is in defence and midfield while the attack has more questions than answers.

And when you are a smaller country needing everything to go right for you, your biggest name and best player having the sort of stinker all tournament that Federico Valverde did basically buries you. Similarly Darwin Nuñez, all flailing limbs and unfulfilled potential, did not have the sort of campaign you need when you’ve just become a free agent.

There is no real need to dwell on Fernando Muslera’s performances, but any team would underperform if their veteran keeper made errors that led to goals in three consecutive games. Who would have thought that Luis Suarez would be more famous for making saves over his World Cup career than Muslera, who was taken off at half-time in Guadalajara and has likely played his last Uruguay game.

open image in gallery Marcelo Bielsa delivers a crazy interview after Uruguay’s elimination ( Reuters )

Last week, a group of senior players including Manuel Ugarte, who went off injured in Guadalajara with a serious-looking injury, Rodrigo Bentancur and Valverde had approached Bielsa about changing the team’s tactics, reducing the intensity of training and imploring him to play a more counter-attacking style in the crunch fixture with Spain.

Once again, Bielsa declined. The resultant defeat was now almost certainly his last match in charge.

The future is going to look different.

Uruguay do at least have the privilege of playing in the South American qualifiers, where in the days of 48-team tournaments it’s pretty difficult not to make it to the big dance. Six of the 10 nations from CONMEBOL are in the USA — Bolivia lost a playoff — and it’s incredibly rare for Uruguay to not be among the South American group.

So they can expect to be back in four years but with a group of players, and coaching staff, that does things a little differently.

Some of the older talent will not return and younger prospects will be introduced. In attack, there is hope in the shape of Joaquin Lavega. He and Santiago Homenchenko, a midfielder by trade, but who Bielsa also liked as a marauding central defender, have both been called up before and now seem like obvious key pieces during the next cycle.

open image in gallery Federico Valverde comes off with Marcelo Bielsa looking on ( Getty )

But they must for once look forward, not back.

Last year in Montevideo there was a fancy drinks reception celebrating the 75th anniversary of Uruguay’s second World Cup win. The Maracanazo, their historic defeat of Brazil in the final game of that tournament, probably represents the country’s most famous moment on a global stage in any sphere, not just sport.

Those two World Cup wins are now generations ago, and while there aren’t delusions of grandeur here, sandwiched as they are between two giants and aware of their own limitations, those ancient glories never die but they can only fuel you for so long.

Perhaps the miracle all along was that this country, the size of Wales, has always been able to keep pace with the biggest fish, but right now it feels like they are drowning.

Britney Spears’ sons, Sean Preston Federline and Jayden James Federline, made their modeling debut Friday on a Paris Fashion Week runway, but their mom wasn’t in the crowd.

Her eldest son Sean Preston, 20, was pictured strutting the runway in a long black silk jacket with a matching black shirt and tie paired with jeans at the Vetements Menswear Spring/Summer 2027 show.

Jayden, 19, walked the runway sporting a pair of faded blue jeans with a fitted white tank top and brown leather loafers.

The “Toxic” singer’s sons were also joined on the runway by three-time Oscar-nominated actor Sharon Stone, who wore a white tailored suit and a black shirt.

Britney Spears has not made any public appearances after she pleaded guilty to driving under the influence following a March incident in Ventura County, California.

open image in gallery Jayden James Federline walking in the Vetements Spring/Summer 2027 show at Paris Fashion Week ( Getty )

open image in gallery Sean Preston Federline walking in the Vetements Spring/Summer 2027 fashion show on June 26 ( Getty )

After the arrest, she made a social media post about her “spiritual journey” and meeting “many new beautiful people” in a new chapter of her life.

“I’m so damn thankful to my friends and so many new beautiful people I have met through my spiritual journey… all a blessing in disguise,” she said at the time.

She said she still has to learn how to “be kind to myself and the way I speak to myself.”

“It’s a never ending journey and sometimes I just stop, look up and say wow God I think that was you and smile on!!!!” she continued.

open image in gallery Britney Spears recently spoke about needing to ‘be kind to myself and the way I speak to myself’ ( Invision/AP )

The “Toxic” singer made the post less than a week after she pleaded guilty to the DUI charge. After her arrest, her representative confirmed she had voluntarily checked herself into a treatment center.

The rep told The Independent after the arrest that “long overdue change” needed to occur in the singer’s life.

“Hopefully, she can get the help and support she needs during this difficult time,” the statement continued. “Her boys are going to be spending time with her. Her loved ones are going to come up with an overdue needed plan to set her up for success for well being.”

The singer reunited with her sons three weeks on from the arrest, sharing a picture of them enjoying time together aboard a yacht.

Spears and her ex-husband Kevin Federline married in Los Angeles in 2004, and welcomed their two sons in 2005 and 2006.

The singer has largely stepped back from her music career, having not toured in nearly eight years or released an album in almost a decade.

Her conservatorship, which lasted almost 14 years, was dissolved in 2021, allowing her to regain control of her life and finances. She later published the bestselling memoir, The Woman in Me.

The record-breaking heatwave gripping the UK should act as a “wake-up call” for Britain to urgently prepare for a Mediterranean climate, experts have warned – with such extreme heat set to happen “again and again”.

Hundreds of schools were forced to close and three NHS trusts declared critical incidents this week as temperature records for June were shattered for three days in a row, with mercury topping 37.3C in Santon Downham, Suffolk, on Friday.

Extreme heat warnings have been extended overnight into Sunday for much of the country, and more than 800 flights were delayed at London’s Gatwick and Heathrow airports as the heatwave turned to thunderstorms.

The deadly heat dome is now moving east to mainland Europe, where temperatures are set to soar above 40C with records broken in Denmark and Slovakia, while roads in Germany are buckling under the strain as it reached a provisional record high of 41.5C. Hundreds of people are believed to have been killed. Some 327 fatalities in Spain are thought to be linked to the extreme heat, while at least 55 people have died in France.

Emma Howard Boyd, chair of the independent National Heat Risk Commission (NHRC), said the stifling temperatures are not a one-off, warning: “This is something that we are going to see happening again and again.”

open image in gallery Record June temperatures were broken for three days in a row this week ( AFP/Getty )

She said the heatwave should “absolutely” act as “a wake-up call” for Britain to upgrade its infrastructure to withstand higher temperatures alongside work to tackle carbon emissions.

“Some argue we should focus less on reaching net zero and more on adapting to climate change,” she said.

“But adaptation without mitigation is like bailing out a boat while drilling more holes in the hull. We have to do both.”

The NHRC, based at the Grantham Research Institute on Climate Change and the Environment at the London School of Economics and Political Science, was established earlier this year in the wake of a July 2022 heatwave, which saw temperatures in Britain exceed 40C for the first time in recorded history.

Nearly 3,000 Britons died from heat-related causes that summer as runways softened, rails buckled and hospital IT systems shut down amid the sweltering heat.

open image in gallery A man in Berlin as the deadly heatwave moves east to mainland Europe ( Reuters )

National upgrades to mitigate against higher temperatures and flash flooding, which often follows heatwaves, must now be “top of the agenda” alongside reducing carbon emissions, Ms Howard Boyd said.

“We either have a chance to build in that resilience or lock in future vulnerability,” she told The Independent.

Urging Britons to start thinking about measures to make their homes more heat safe, like installing shutters or planting trees nearby, she added: “We need to start thinking about our climate becoming a Mediterranean climate.”

As thermometers hit 30C in some areas of Britain on Saturday, more than 400 flights arriving at or departing from Heathrow were delayed, according to tracker FlightAware, and another 400 in and out of Gatwick.

Meanwhile, a 22-year-old man’s body has been recovered from a river after it was reported he got into difficulty during the heatwave, police said. Brody Leach’s body was recovered from the River Severn in Shrewsbury, Shropshire, on Saturday morning, West Mercia Police said. The area around the riverside where searches were taking place has reopened following searches for Mr Leach after he entered the river on Friday and then got into difficulty.

Elsewhere, officers searching for a missing 15-year-old boy last seen in the water at Testwood Lakes near Southampton have now found a body, Hampshire Police said. “The boy’s family have been informed, and formal identification has taken place. His family are being supported by specially-trained officers,” the force said in a statement.

The two deaths bring the number of people to have lost their lives in water during the recent June heatwave to three after a 50-year-old man was pronounced dead on Wednesday afternoon at Aberavon beach after getting into difficulty while swimming in the sea off the south coast of Wales.

According to the Met Office, summers could be between 1C and 6C warmer by 2070 and up to 60 per cent drier, depending on the region. Spanish plumes, which bring hot conditions, could become more intense, creating even hotter weather and more intense downpours during summer thunderstorms.

The Green Alliance, a London-based think tank, said that higher temperatures are the reality of climate change and people are paying the price, after more died in the heatwave of July 2022 than were killed on the roads that year.

Director of politics, Holly Brazier Tope, said: “We built and planned our homes and communities for a UK that isn’t this hot, and right now, people are paying the price.

open image in gallery Shops were forced to cover fridges to keep items cool during the heat ( AFP/Getty )

“Schools are closing early, NHS appointments are being cancelled, trains are running late. This is the reality of climate change on our doorstep, and successive governments have left people to face it unprotected. Without urgent action, 92 per cent of existing homes could overheat by mid-century and heat-related deaths could rise to 10,000 a year.”

She added: “This is not a future threat. It is here, it is now, and it is the consequence of inaction. This government must respond fast with a systemic, nationwide response that delivers smarter planning, community resilience, protection now and net zero for the future.”

Gareth Redmond-King, the international lead at Energy & Climate Intelligence Unit, said that aiming for net zero emissions is the only route to halt climate change and “stop everything getting ever hotter and more dangerous”.

“But we need to adapt too; the most vulnerable in our society, in nurseries, schools, hospitals and care homes are having their health and lives put at risk as these dangerous extremes get worse,” he told The Independent.

“By working with other countries to hit net zero by 2050, someone in their fifties today could see temperature rises stop, such that extremes aren’t edging ever higher in the 40Cs in their retirement.

“In short, the weather this week should serve as a wake-up call for us all on net zero. The quicker we get there, the less likely it is that we trip tipping points, like the collapse of the Amazon rainforest.”

A government spokesperson said: “We are working across government to carefully consider the Climate Change Committee's latest recommendations in relation to climate adaptation.

“We are already taking action to help safeguard people, livelihoods and our natural environment by investing in clean power, ensuring new residential buildings are designed to minimise unwanted heat from the sun and launching the Local Authority Climate Service, which provides local authorities with easy access to tailored information to support adaptation planning.

“During this week’s extreme heat, people should pay attention to the latest alerts and guidance issued for their area by UKHSA.”

News.title: Teen went to hunt registered sex offenders in his neighborhood armed with BB gun, police say
News.content:
The latest headlines from our reporters across the US sent straight to your inbox each weekday Your briefing on the latest headlines from across the US Your briefing on the latest headlines from across the US Email * SIGN UP I would like to be emailed about offers, events and updates from The Independent. Read our Privacy notice

A teenager in California allegedly used the state’s sex offender registry to identify and confront people he believed were listed on it, threatening and shooting at them with a BB gun, according to a report.

The suspect, who turned 18 this week, was 17 at the time of the incidents in March, the East Bay Times reported Thursday, citing police and court records.

The teen allegedly walked around Walnut Creek carrying a BB-style gun and a handwritten list of names pulled from Megan’s Law, a public registry created after the murder of 7-year-old Megan Kanka, which provides offenders’ photos and addresses to the public. He then confronted, threatened and fired at people he believed were registered sex offenders, officials said.

He was arrested March 15 on suspicion of brandishing a weapon and assault with a firearm, according to court and police records reviewed by the outlet. The case remains under investigation in juvenile court, and his identity has not been released due to privacy laws, EBT reported.

The suspect is also reportedly under investigation for a separate April incident involving alleged drug distribution to minors.

open image in gallery The California teen accused of the crimes reportedly turned 18 this week ( Getty/iStock )

In April, a female student at Los Lomas High School was hospitalized after unknowingly ingesting a significant dose of cannabis in a sandwich provided by a male student, according to EBT.

Investigators later identified the same teen as a suspected seller of marijuana and other drugs. They allegedly recovered Instagram messages showing him offering marijuana and psychedelic mushrooms to other teenagers and discussing bulk sales.

A search of his Walnut Creek home last month reportedly turned up $1,300 in cash and packaged cannabis edibles similar to those linked to the earlier incident, according to EBT.

It is unclear whether the 18-year-old will face criminal charges in either investigation, according to the outlet.

The Independent has contacted the Walnut Creek Police Department and Los Lomas High School for comment.

News.title: Humbled England staring at rare home series defeat
News.content:
It is going to require a run chase for the ages by a humbled England team to avoid a rare home series defeat at the worst possible time for those in charge.

Trent Bridge was where it all began for Bazball in 2022; a lifetime ago when Jonny Bairstow smoked a 77-ball hundred as England strode triumphantly to 299 to stun New Zealand. They had had nothing to lose in those innocent, adrenalin-fuelled days at the start of their great adventure with Ben Stokes and Brendon McCullum.

How times change. Now they are staring at a sizeable target on a pitch that has changed character, with so much pressure on the decision makers at the heart of an England dogged by disciplinary issues and burdened by their best players out of form or low on confidence. With New Zealand 120 for three, the lead 204 at the end of day three, it will be a formidable achievement for England to steal victory considering the weight on their shoulders.

Fail and they will lose a home series of at least three Tests for the first time since 2012. After the psychodrama of the past three weeks, who knows what will happen to the captain, coach or director of cricket if New Zealand go on to win their fourth series in England.

A third day arm wrestle ended with New Zealand enjoying the upper hand because England were not good enough to make the most two clear opportunities, one in the morning session and one in the evening.

Restarting on 223 for two with Jacob Bethell and Joe Root at the crease, England were in position to overhaul or at least come close to New Zealand’s under-par first innings 438. Bethell and Root failed to add to their overnight scores, England lost three for 10 in the first half an hour and eight for 131 in total to concede an 84-run lead.

News.title: George Russell takes dramatic pole after late Max Verstappen crash
News.content:
Would Russell’s pole lap be allowed? There was some doubt over whether it was single or double yellows which had been waved at the drivers immediately after Verstappen’s crash. Even if it was just single yellows, had Russell backed off sufficiently?

The British driver faced an anxious wait to discover his fate before stewards decided there was no investigation necessary. Apparently it was just single waved yellows, with the doubles only coming out 15 seconds or so later. And Russell had backed off 100m or so before the corner.

“It was a big lift,” he said in his immediate post-qualifying TV interview, before his pole was confirmed. “I was five tenths up when I went into the last corner, and ended up two-and-a-half tenths up.”

Russell later added that he was glad “common sense prevailed”. “It was a corner where you can see quite a lot,” he argued in the main FIA press conference. “I did a huge lift [compared to previous laps] and, as it was a single yellow, I could see there was no danger. [Verstappen] was so far off the track.”

Perhaps Russell’s luck is changing. Having suffered so many body blows this season, from qualifying gremlins in China, to the timing of the safety car in Japan, to his power unit failure in Canada, to the pitlane speeding penalty that never should have been in Monaco, that is now two race weekends in a row in which he has enjoyed a fair dollop of luck.

Not only did Russell manage to get his lap in – it was his best of the session by a mile, and came right after Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff came on the radio to tell him to believe in himself and “just drive” – his team-mate and championship leader Kimi Antonelli mistakenly backed out of his.

News.title: Dembele silences critics with stunning 25-minute hat-trick to sink Norway
News.content:
The game has been billed as Erling Haaland vs Kylian Mbappé but Norway vs France will also determine top spot in Group I.

France are strong favourites to claim it after two victories and seven goals, and only a Norway victory in Foxborough, Massachusetts will depose them.

There have also been plenty of goals in Norway’s wins over Iraq and Senegal, with Haaland scoring four and Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard providing a couple of assists.

Mbappé is also on four goals, one behind tournament top scorer Lionel Messi, and this is the first international in which Mbappé and Haaland have faced each other.

Norway has been ear-marked as tournament dark horses for months, but their talent is front-loaded and their defence will face a stern examination against the speed and dexterity of France’s attack. Should Norway fail to win and finish second in the group, they will play Ivory Coast in the round of 32.

Didier Deschamps will not be on the touchline after travelling back to France following the death of his mother.

Assistant manager Guy Stéphan will stand in for Deschamps and changes are expected in the starting XI.

William Saliba will be rested as he continues to nurse back discomfort, replaced by Crystal Palace defender Maxence Lacroix, who has been strongly linked with a move to Chelsea in recent days.

Elsewhere in the team, Aurélien Tchouaméni is expected to come in for Adrien Rabiot and Chelsea full-back Malo Gusto could make his first start of the tournament. As things stand, France will play Sweden in the next round if they top the group though there is scope for that to change.

In the other game in the group, Senegal are the only team currently in third-place on zero points, and know they need to beat Iraq to stand a chance of progressing as one of the eight-best teams in that mini-league.

Three points for Senegal would lift them above Scotland in that table, and push Steve Clarke’s team closer to elimination. Scotland’s exit will not be confirmed by close of play tonight, but it could come early tomorrow morning after the conclusion of Group H and Group G, where Cape Verde’s and Belgium’s fixtures are relevant.



Full team news on the way shortly, and we will have goal updates from Senegal vs Iraq.

News.title: Duckett finds form of old to get England back into contest
News.content:
Hello and welcome to live, over-by-over coverage of the second day of the deciding Test between England and New Zealand. For much of day one England were staring at a stinker for the ages, but a thoroughly admirable fightback (imagine summoning the energy to do anything worthwhile when the opposition are 317/0 in that heat) has given them a sniff.

We’ve said it before, we’ll say it again: this is a big first hour. New Zealand will resume on 361/4, with the second new ball only 4.1 overs old. They have a long tail, too, and if England start well they could roll New Zealand for an under-par score.

It feels a little perverse to type that when they are 361/4, but the Trent Bridge wicket is a belter and both teams will be mindful of New Zealand’s last Test on this ground four years ago. They were 405/4 early on day two yet still lost by five wickets when Jonny Bairstow went berserk on the final day.

Tim Southee, who was in that New Zealand team, is now England’s bowling coach and was full of praise for the hard yakka they put in on a sweltering day.

“It’s Test cricket, it’s hard, and on a surface like that it’s particularly hard. But we got some rewards late in the day,” he said. “We sit here now with a couple (more wickets) and we’re coming tomorrow with the new ball and a bit of energy from the bowlers.

“Test cricket is played over five days and you’ve got to be able to believe you’re in a position where all three results are possible. We sit here after day one with New Zealand four down, two new batters in, a nightwatchman at one end and a new ball in hand. It’s exciting.”

A lot more exciting than it promised to be when New Zealand were 317/0.

News.title: Hunger crisis warning as paramilitary activity escalates around new Sudanese city
News.content:
A looming paramilitary assault on the Sudanese city of El Obeid threatens to deepen the country’s “already catastrophic hunger crisis”, the World Food Programme has warned.

The UN agency said reports of “substantial military activity” around the city, coupled with escalating drone attacks, risk unleashing “a new wave of violence and mass displacement” in El Obeid, the strategic capital of North Kordofan state in central Sudan, which has become the new epicentre in the country’s four year war.

An estimated 62 per cent of Sudan’s population, around 29 million people, are already acutely ​food insecure, according to the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC), the global hunger monitor, which has also confirmed famine in two areas.

The WFP is already providing aid to over 100,000 people in El Obeid, where hundreds of thousands of people are enduring siege conditions and diminishing access to food, water, healthcare as escalating drone strikes target basic services.

The UN agency is now rapidly pre-positioning aid to support up to 250,000 people who may be forced to flee if the situation deteriorates further.

Abdallah Alwardat, WFP’s Country Director for Sudan, said: “We must act swiftly to save lives as per our humanitarian mandate…This action, however, comes at a cost”.

He warned that the agency was diverting food stocks originally intended to be pre-positioned ahead of the rainy season, adding: “In September, we will run out of food for our emergency operations across the country, which today reaches just one in five people in need of food assistance for survival”.

Sports.title: Who is Panama vs England referee Abdulrahman Al-Jassim? Meet the Qatari official taking charge of World Cup 2026 clash

BIG ABS Who is Panama vs England referee Abdulrahman Al-Jassim? Meet the Qatari official taking charge of World Cup 2026 clash

ENGLAND face Panama tonight in their final World Cup group stage match, and fans are eager to find out who is officiating the Three Lions’ pivotal match.

Abdulrahman Al-Jassim is the man in the middle at MetLife Stadium – he previously took charge of Portugal’s 1-1 draw with DR Congo at this year’s tournament.





Who is Abdulrahman Al-Jassim?

Al-Jassim was born in Qatar in 1987.

He became a FIFA registered official in 2013 and was one of the referees for the 2017 Under-20 World Cup in South Korea.

The 35-year-old was later appointed as a video assistant referee for the 2018 World Cup in Russia.

Two years on, Al-Jassim was selected to referee the AFC Champions League final which saw South Korean side Ulsan Hyundai beat Iranian team Persepolis 2-1.

He later switched continents, refereeing at the Gold Cup in the United States.

In 2019, Al-Jassim completed a trio of Qatari officials who took charge of the Club World Cup final which saw Liverpool snatch the win against Flamengo in extra time.

He was appointed the only Qatari official in his home World Cup in 2022.

Al-Jassim took charge of two matches at the tournament, the first being between USA and Wales in the group stage before officiating the third place playoff between Croatia and Morocco.

Sports.title: Chelsea ‘line up shock Granit Xhaka transfer with World Cup star, 33, ready to accept any condition to join’
Sports.content:
CHELSEA have lined up a shock move to bring Granit Xhaka to Stamford Bridge, according to reports.

The Switzerland World Cup star enjoyed a stellar year back in the Premier League playing for Sunderland.





Xhaka, 33, played 36 times for the Black Cats last season, including 34 times in the English top flight as the club finished an impressive seventh place and earned Europa League football immediately after their promotion from the Championship.

The former Arsenal captain – who had that title stripped away by Unai Emery following a public spat with Gooners before redeeming himself at the North London club under Mikel Arteta – is said to have verbally accepted personal terms over a move.

According to Sky Germany reporter Florian Plettenberg, the Blues are in contact with Sunderland as they attempt to strike a deal.

Bidding for Xhaka represents a shift away from Chelsea‘s previous transfer strategy under BlueCo which saw them hoover up a swathe of promising talent while neglecting already-proven assets.

That plan unravelled this season and saw the West Londoners finish a lowly-tenth place in the league.

However, following the appointment of ex-Bayer Leverkusen boss Xabi Alonso – who worked with Xhaka when the German club won an unbeaten Bundesliga and DFB Pokal double – it was revealed Chelsea would be shifting their transfer strategy to more ready-made players.

Sky Sports’ Keith Downie claims Sunderland consider their captain to be not for sale, while reports in Italy have stated Chelsea will offer £26million to land the midfield veteran.

Xhaka, who has played every minute of his countries World Cup campaign so far, has experience in abundance, something Chelsea’s young squad were accused of lacking last season.



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

The move to land Xhaka also coincides with the expected departure of Enzo Fernandez, who is being targeted by Real Madrid.

Xhaka spent seven seasons playing for Chelsea’s London rivals Arsenal between 2016 and 2023, playing a total of 297 games, scoring 23 goals and adding 29 assists with two FA Cup‘s in his trophy cabinet.

In terms of personal accolades he was also a two-time winner of the Gunners’ Player of the Year award.

He left Arsenal in 2023 for a deal worth just over £21m to join Alonso at Bayer, where they won the club a first ever Bundesliga title to break the cycle of Bayern Munich dominance which had gripped Germany.



Speaking in November 2024, TNT Sports pundit Raphael Honigstein said of Xhaka’s time under Alonso: “We always knew that Xhaka had a big personality. That he was an important dressing room voice and a real leader.

“But now, his football has gone to another level in the last couple of years and I think that is because of the influence of [Alonso and Mikel Arteta] as experienced former central midfielders.

“It is clear that with Alonso playing or taking part in many sessions himself, and still being the best player on the pitch, you can pick up so many things if you’re willing…

“I think that there’s a reason why he was captain at Arsenal. There’s a reason why Leverkusen were desperate to get him in. Alonso effectively built a team around him to a certain extent.

“Xhaka has been one reason why they’ve managed to instil this togetherness and real team mentality that the past Leverkusen teams haven’t always been able to produce, because of their nature as sort of a stepping stone for many players.



“He’s one of the main reasons why Leverkusen have now gone from being a very good team to being a superb side.”

After two seasons playing in Leverkusen, Xhaka returned to England with newly-promoted Sunderland in a deal worth £13m.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

It is claimed the Swiss star always wanted a move back to the capital, with West Ham interested at the time before they decided against pursuing a move.

Elsewhere, Chelsea are eyeing a new recruit in central defence, with Crystal Palace‘s Maxence Lacroix reportedly the subject of an enquiry.

Sports.title: ‘I thought it was AI’ – Fans left stunned after seeing view from 53,529-seater World Cup’s most beautiful stadium
Sports.content:
FANS have been left speechless after a jaw-dropping photo from the World Cup sparked claims it looked “too perfect to be real”.

The incredible image was taken inside the 53,529-capacity Estadio Monterrey before South Africa’s 1-0 win against South Korea in Mexico.





With the stadium packed to the rafters and towering green mountains rising dramatically beyond the open roof, supporters hailed it as one of the most beautiful football grounds on the planet.

The snap quickly spread across social media, leaving many in awe of the view and racking up hundreds of thousands of views.

One fan wrote: “First time I think it’s AI. Haha but this is real. It’s very beautiful.”

Another said: “What a beautiful sight.”



A third added: “Imagine watching football there, wow.”

The stadium, home to Liga MX giants Monterrey, has become one of the standout venues at the expanded 2026 World Cup.

Its dramatic setting, nestled beneath the Sierra Madre mountains, has provided a spectacular backdrop throughout the tournament.

The game matched the setting as South Africa beat South Korea 1-0 to reach the knockout stages of the tournament for the first time.



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

Thapelo Maseko’s 63rd-minute winner helped South Africa leapfrog their opponents to finish second in the group.

If the football wasn’t enough to impress fans, the unforgettable scenery certainly was.

With the knockout stages soon underway, the spectacular stadium is set to remain one of the tournament’s biggest attractions both on and off the pitch.

Sports.title: How England lined up last time they faced Panama including 4 World Cup 2026 stars & ace playing in Brazil under new name
Sports.content:
ENGLAND’S World Cup campaign has a sense of deja vu thanks to facing some familiar opponents.

The Three Lions opened up against Croatia – a thrilling 4-2 win – a rival fans have become all too accustomed with, having played them in the opener of Euro 2020 and in the semi-finals of the 2018 World Cup.





Ghana, who held England to a 0-0 bore draw, were an opponent England hadn’t faced for well over a decade.

But like the Black Stars, Panama are a nation being played against for only the second time.

The previous match against the Canal Men came in 2018, with it being the second match Gareth Southgate‘s team had in the group stage – and the last time England won their second game at a major tournament.

This time around, Panama are the third and final group game.



But there are a host of other changes since the last clash between the 1966 world champions and Central American nation.

For starters, there is a new manager in the Three Lions dugout in the form of Thomas Tuchel, who like Southgate in 2018, is taking charge of his first international tournament.

The game played out on 24 June 2018 ended in a resounding 6-1 win for England, marking the first time the nation scored as many goals in a major tournament.

Harry Kane led the way that day by scoring a hat-trick.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

He was joined on the scoresheet by John Stones, who grabbed a brace, and Jesse Lingard.

Eight years later, Lingard plays with a new name on the back of his shirt.

The former Manchester United star, 33, now goes by JLingz while playing in Brazil for Corinthians.

His midfield partners for the day were Ruben Loftus-Cheek and Jordan Henderson, the latter of whom has returned to the England set-up under Tuchel, but is unlikely to feature at the tournament.



The only other star from the team then was Jordan Pickford in goal.

Elsewhere, Harry Maguire missed out on selection, while Kyle Walker and Kieran Trippier both retired from international duty.

Ashley Young, who played left wing-back during that tournament, hung up his boots entirely after the end of this season.

Former Chelsea and Fulham star Loftus-Cheek, now at AC Milan, played and picked up England’s sole yellow card in the game.



Meanwhile, Kane’s forward partner, Raheem Sterling, is without a club after his Feyenoord contract expired.

Sports.title: Liverpool’s Cody Gakpo and girlfriend announce tragic loss of their baby as star competes at World Cup
Sports.content:
CODY GAKPO’s girlfriend has announced the tragic news that the couple have lost their child during pregnancy.

The Liverpool winger has been in the US in recent weeks competing at the World Cup with the Netherlands national team.





But now he and his long-term partner, model Noa van der Bij, will have to navigate this awful news together after she confirmed the loss on her social media pages.

She wrote: “With broken hearts, we share the devastating news that our baby boy passed away during pregnancy.

“Thank you for your love and support.”

The family only revealed the pregnancy in May, though van der Bij at that point had already been pregnant for months.

Heartbreakingly, they had already picked out a name, with van der Bij adding the touching message: “Elijah Raphael Gakpo. Forever loved. Forever our son.”

Elijah was van der Bij and Gakpo‘s second pregnancy, after welcoming their first child, Samuel Seth Gakpo, in 2024.

She revealed that the family lit a candle in a church in honour of Elijah, adding that they also bumped into another child, who shared the unborn baby’s name.

Van der Bij referred to the moment with hope, saying: “There could not have been a more beautiful sign from god. He reminded us that our little boy is never far away.”



Where to find help after a stillbirth? A stillbirth is when a baby is born dead after 24 completed weeks of pregnancy. It happens in around 1 in every 200 births in England. The emotional and physical impact on a woman is incredibly intense. Alongside the physical recovery of childbirth, mothers often face immense grief, overwhelming loneliness, guilt, depression, and Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD). This trauma can be equally as severe for women who face the heartbreak of a late termination for medical reasons (TFMR). If you or a loved one are going through this, you do not have to carry the weight alone. Here are the UK’s leading baby loss charities, who offer free, confidential, and judgment-free support: Sands (Stillbirth and Neonatal Death Society) Provide a safe, understanding community for anyone touched by the death of a baby, whether the loss happened recently or decades ago.

They offer direct emotional support through a dedicated national helpline and online chat.

How to Contact:

Helpline: 0808 164 3332 (Free to call)

Email: helpline@sands.org.uk

Website: sands.org.uk Tommy’s A non-judgmental support helpline staffed entirely by specialised midwives who are deeply experienced in bereavement, medical complications, and TFMR.

They provide practical advice on registering a baby, navigating a return to work, and coping with the anxiety of a future pregnancy.

How to contact:

Helpline: 0800 0147 800 (Free to call, Mon-Fri, 9am–5pm)

Email: midwife@tommys.org

Website: tommys.org

Both van der Bij and Elijah were in attendance in the US to support Gakpo during his World Cup opener against Japan last week.

But his imminent future at the tournament is naturally uncertain in the wake of such devastating news.

Sports.title: England vs Panama LIVE - Team news leaked ahead of crucial World Cup group match
Sports.content:
England face already-eliminated Panama tonight as they aim to finish top and ensure a favourable draw in the round of 32, but Thomas Tuchel is paying for some squad decisions

England vs Panama LIVE - Team news as Tuchel makes FOUR changes with Rogers and Saka set to start

England's group stage campaign comes to an end on Saturday night when they face World Cup minnows Panama.

The Three Lions need to show clear improvements from Tuesday's lacklustre 0-0 draw with Ghana, which served as a reality check following their impressive 4-2 win against Croatia that kickstarted their tournament.

Thomas Tuchel, though, has a number of injury worries ahead of the game in New Jersey, with Reece James' tournament potentially over unless England make the latter stages. Tuchel has also had to address concerns over Declan Rice and Elliot Anderson.

Tuchel did confirm that Bukayo Saka is ready to start after coming off the bench in the opening two matches because of a long-term Achilles tendinitis complaint.

England have met Panama at the World Cup previously, with that game coming eight years ago in Russia. Harry Kane scored a hat-trick in a 6-1 hammering.

The Three Lions face Panama at 10pm tonight, with Croatia taking on Ghana in the other Group L clash at the same time. Stay tuned as Mirror Football keeps you across all of the build-up.

Sports.title: England fans party in New Jersey ahead of Panama as Three Lions already through to knockout stages
Sports.content:
England fans party in New Jersey ahead of Panama as Three Lions already through to knockout stages

England face Panama tonight in New Jersey and victory for Thomas Tuchel's side would almost certainly guarantee top spot of Group L of the World Cup 2026

View 5 Images England Fans at the American Dream Fanzone in NJ ahead of Englands last group L match in the 2026 FIFA World Cup

England fans are living the American Dream in New Jersey as they party in a World Cup fanzone for the match against Panama.

‌



Neil Diamond's Three Lions anthem 'Sweet Caroline' was playing as fans lined up behind their Bristol City, Huddersfield Town, Middlesbrough FC and Pennsylvania Owls flags.

‌



In the Yard House Pub inside the giant American Dream fanzone, 2.5 pint, $16 (£12) ales were being served to thirsty England fans as they chanted terrace anthems and enjoyed the World Cup atmosphere with supporters from Panama and across the United States.

‌



For some, it was the end of their World Cup journey. They told how they were heading home this week, with Thomas Tuchel's side already through to the knockout phase.

England vs Panama LIVE - Team news leaked ahead of crucial World Cup group match READ MORE :

View 5 Images England Fan at the American Dream Fanzone

'We are having fun'

Others had combined the football with darts and a trip to see Luke Littler defeated 8-7 by Luke Humphries in a thriller at Madison Square Garden on Friday night.

‌



Bristol City fans Richard Iles, 55, and Andrew Rodgers, 56, were at the end of a £30,000 trip to see all of the group games before heading home.

Richard, who also travelled to Qatar for the 2022 World Cup, said: "We have really enjoyed the experience. The tickets are too expensive, the travel is too expensive, everything is too expensive but we are having fun. What do you do as a fan? You either pay or you don't come.

"We have done all three group games and Dallas was such a great game with a great atmosphere. Then we had second game syndrome but we have really made the most of it."

‌



View 5 Images England Fans at the American Dream Fanzone, Richard Iles (left) and Andrew Rodgers

England fans spend £15,000 each

Andrew, who is also retired, added: "Qatar was so different because everything was so easy - all the stadiums were within an hour and a half of our hotel and the Metro system was brilliant.

‌



"We paid 12,000 US dollars each for the package here because it provided tickets to each game, hotels and transfers. But the flights home are on top of that so it will have been around £15,000 each.

"Last night at the darts, the ticket was $123 and a pint was £18; yet there were still 5,000 people in there and almost all of them were English. It was a great match and perfectly timed for the football."

Wolves fan Braden Webb, 20, of Stafford, travelling with his dad Paul, 63, told how they met US fans at the Ghana game. They ended up getting a lift to the stadium and 'tailgating' with Ghana fans - a US tradition where BBQ food is served from the back of vehicles in the car park before the game.

‌



University of Birmingham student Braden, who is training to be a PE teacher, joked: "Can you imagine doing that at Molineux? We were also sitting with the opposition fans and many Americans who were cheering for Ghana. That was grinding my gears. But the stadium was amazing and it was a great experience."

View 5 Images Left to Right Panama fans Katie Krech and Geraldine Villarreal before the Panama England match

Panama fans were excited that their most important player, Carrasquilla, who has yet to play a minute at this World Cup, was likely to be fit. In 2024, Carrasquilla became the first Panamanian named Concacaf men's player of the year.

‌



He trained as a hairdresser in his youth and was giving his team-mates a trim by the time he made his senior debut aged 16 for Panamanian side Tauro.

Carrasquilla still occasionally cuts hair at the local barber when he is visiting family back home. He had promised to shave his head if Panama wins the World Cup.

Panama fan Geraldine Villarreal, 25, had travelled from Fort Lauderdale, Florida with her friend Katie Kreh, 31, to see the game.

‌



Geraldine said: "We know that we are out so we are here to have a good time and just sample the atmosphere.

"We met when we were both dating Englishmen in America, and we are both working in Florida.

"We have a soft spot for England but obviously we are biased."

‌



View 5 Images England Fans at the American Dream Fanzone

'I am just buzzing to be here'

Tiffany McKenna, 33, originally from Whitley Bay, North Tyneside but now living in Houston, Texas, told how her twin sister Alex has to put bets on for her back home in the UK because it is illegal in her home state.

She joked: "You cannot gamble in Texas. We could not get tickets for the Croatia game in Dallas which was so frustrating.

‌



"So I am just buzzing to be here."

The American Dream shopping complex, opposite the MetLife Stadium - renamed the New York/New Jersey stadium for the tournament - has been transformed into a giant fanzone.

It served drinks to England and Panama fans before the 5pm kickoff local time and then showed the game for those without tickets.

‌



A "major hub for football and soccer experiences," it offers massive screens, celebrity appearances, and entertainment.

The stadium's capacity has been reduced from 87,157 to just under 80,000 for the tournament.

It was expected to be at least half full of Three Lions supporters from the UK and across the US.

Sports.title: Liverpool star Cody Gakpo left heartbroken as baby son dies during pregnancy
Sports.content:
Liverpool star Cody Gakpo left heartbroken as baby son dies during pregnancy

Liverpool forward Cody Gakpo and his partner announced that they were expecting their second child together in May

View 3 Images Cody Gakpo's baby son has died during pregnancy (Image: Getty Images)

Cody Gakpo's partner Noa van der Bij has confirmed that their son, Elijah, has died during pregnancy. The Liverpool forward and his girlfriend were expecting their second son and confirmed the news in May.

‌



The 27-year-old is currently at the World Cup on international duty with Holland while his girlfriend, Noa, is in the United States to support the Reds attacker. In May, the two shared a heart-warming Instagram post that they were expecting a second child due in October, after their son Samuel was born in 2024.

‌



However, in two Instagram stories on Saturday, Van der Bij revealed that the couple had suffered a miscarriage. Noa posted a picture of the two holding hands over a blanket and a knitted hat, along with the caption: "With broken hearts, we share the devastating news that our baby boy passed away during pregnancy. Thank you for your love and support. Elijah Raphael Gakpo Forever loved. Forever our son."

‌



In a follow-up story, she posted a picture of a lit candle in a church with the caption: "We went to church to light a candle. Afterward, we walked to the church playground with our son Samuel. There was only one other child there. His name was Elijah.

"There could not have been a more beautiful sign from God He reminded us that our little boy is never far away."

Man Utd transfer blow as World Cup injury threatens Mateus Fernandes deal READ MORE :

It is unclear when the passing of their son occurred, as Gakpo's partner has posted to social media throughout the summer after Liverpool's season finished.

‌



She posted a carousel of pictures on Instagram at the beginning of June resting a drink on her bump before following up with snaps in Texas and during Oranje's World Cup opener against Japan.

Dutch outlet De Telegraaf reported that Gakpo did not get off the team bus for training four days ago but was later brought by car. The Dutch football federation, KNVB, said at the time he was not late but there was a good reason for it.

3 View 3 Images An Instagram story from Cody Gakpo's girlfriend Noa Van der Bij announced their baby has "passed away during pregnancy". (Image: noavdbij/Instagram) 3 View 3 Images An Instagram story from Cody Gakpo's girlfriend Noa Van der Bij after she confirmed that they had lost their second son during pregnancy. (Image: noavdbij/Instagram)

‌



Liverpool supporters on social media rushed to support the forward and his partner following the devastating news. One account tweeted: "Sending our thoughts, love and condolences to Cody Gakpo and his family following the heartbreaking news of the loss of their baby boy. YNWA."

The tweet, viewed over 213,000 times on X, saw condolences and expressions of support flood in the replies. Another user replied: "No words for this. Just so, so sorry for Cody and his family. This is the kind of pain that puts everything else into perspective.

"We’re with you, Cody. All the love in the world. Take all the time you need. YNWA."

Article continues below

Holland are next in action on June 30 (3am BST) at the World Cup when they take on Morocco at the Monterrey Stadium in Mexico. The winner will face the victors of South Africa and co-host Canada in Houston, Texas on July 4 (6pm BST).

Gakpo has two goals in the tournament so far as he looks to continue his form at international level with Ronald Koeman's side. The 27-year-old starred for Oranje at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar and earned a move to Liverpool on the back of his performances.

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca has started Man City job but awaits confirmation to replace Pep Guardiola
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca has started Man City job but awaits confirmation to replace Pep Guardiola

EXCLUSIVE: Enzo Maresca has already begun doing the ground work as Manchester City's new boss despite the Italian not yet confirmed as Pep Guardiola's replacement

View 2 Images Enzo Maresca is yet to be announced as the next Manchester City boss (Image: (Eddie Keogh/Getty Images))

Enzo Maresca has started his new job as Manchester City boss. The Italian has spent time at the club’s training ground this week, getting used to his new surroundings.

‌



Etihad bosses have still to confirm Maresca as Pep Guardiola’s replacement. Chairman Khaldoon Al-Mubarak has been thrashing out a compensation deal with Chelsea - who sacked Maresca in January.

‌



But Maresca has wasted no time getting started on the impossible task of following in Guardiola’s footsteps. Maresca has been studying data belonging to each member of his squad.

‌



He will use this to devise pre-season training sessions for when the squad returns to the club next month. Some will head back to Manchester later than others, due to the World Cup in North America. Maresca has agreed a three year deal at the Etihad.

Newcastle braced for Man City's next transfer move as club fear summer exodus READ MORE :

And it’s understood he will meet senior club figures next week to discuss what the expectations of him will be. Guardiola decided to stand down last summer.

But he kept the decision private, with only a few members of his inner circle aware he would be leaving 12 months later. City targeted Maresca six months ago, when it became clear he would be available following his dismissal by Chelsea.

‌



Guardiola won a remarkable 20 trophies during his decade of dominance with City, including the Treble in 2023. Maresca knows he will be on a hiding to nothing once the season kicks off.

View 2 Images Enzo Maresca previously served as an assistant to Pep Guardiola (Image: (Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC via Getty Images))

But at least he has been boosted with the news City have struck a British record deal to sign England star Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest for a fee of £116million, which could rise to £130m.

‌



City will embark on their new era without a Guardiola stalwart in Bernardo Silva, who chose to leave upon the expiry of his contract. He's since joined Real Madrid. John Stones has also left the Etihad.

Sports.title: 4 breakout World Cup stars attracting major Premier League transfer interest
Sports.content:
The World Cup is the biggest shop window on the planet. And all Premier League clubs are gazing straight through it right now, with hard cash burning a hole in their pockets.

With the odd exception - Elliot Anderson, Nico Paz, Marc Cucurella - the transfer market has ground to a halt. While all those who will go on to define it later this summer, showcase their skills in North America. It will be an open goal for some, while others will blow their big chance to secure a big move on even dreamier wages.

But World Cups have a reliable habit of presenting the game with a new superstar. Think James Rodriguez in Brazil, Kylian Mbappe in Russia and Enzo Fernandez in Qatar. This latest edition of the greatest show on turf will be no different.

Get the latest World Cup news straight to your inbox by signing up to our Make Football Great Again newsletter now!

‌



Someone who could be about to hit the footballing jackpot is Yan Diomande.

The Ivory Coast winger only joined RB Leipzig 12 months ago for £17.3m, but is expected to be on the move again this summer, for more than five times this amount. Liverpool have shown interest in someone who managed 23 goal contributions in 36 appearances for the Bundesliga side last season.

Diomande, 19, has still to open his account at the World Cup, but has tormented defenders with his blistering pace and sublime dribbling skills. Something not to have gone unnoticed. His versatility is also appealing, meaning Liverpool will have some competition if they decide to sign him.

‌



Leipzig, meanwhile, have wasted no time in exploiting Diomande's success, slapping a price tag of £100m on the teenage sensation.

View 5 Images Yan Diomande has been shining at the World Cup after an excellent season with RB Leipzig (Image: Michael Miller/ISI Photos, ISI Photos via Getty Images)

Another star to have made his mark is Brighton's Yasin Ayari. The attacking midfielder took time to settle on the south coast, following his move from AIK Athens.

But three goals and three assists in 29 appearances last season, offered a glimpse of his talents. And thanks to two impressive goals form outside the penalty area, to help Sweden thrash Tunisia, Ayari has emerged has one of the unheralded stars of the tournament to date.

‌



He's made his mark. But it remains to be seen if this helps secure him a new deal at the Amex Stadium. Ayari, 22, will become a free agent next summer, and with Brighton having a knack of developing young talent to sell on at huge profit, the Seagulls could now be tempted to cash in.

Newcastle and Aston Villa are keeping close tabs on someone who will not be short of offers when he returns to his domestic duties.

View 5 Images Yasin Ayari is a man in demand with only a year left on his Brighton contract (Image: 2026 FIFA)

Another breakout star has been Morocco's Ayyoub Bouaddi. The 18-year-old could have pledged his international allegiance to France, but chose Morocco instead. And the African nation, which reached the semi finals last time out, should be delighted Bouaddi did.

‌



The teenager impressed on his World Cup debut, against Brazil no less, helping his side earn a creditable 1-1 draw. He has since earned rich praise for showing maturity and composure beyond his years in the engine room of midfield.

Chelsea, who are resigned to losing Enzo Fernandez to Real Madrid, have earmarked him as a possible replacement for the Argentine World Cup winner. While Arsenal and Manchester City are also monitoring his development.

View 5 Images Ayyoub Bouaddi is moving closer to an exit from Lille (Image: Daniela Porcelli/Getty Images)

View 5 Images Antonio Nusa of Norway is another RB Leipzig star showing his talent (Image: Ulrik Pedersen/NurPhoto)

‌



And let's not forget Norway's Antonio Nusa.

Erling Haaland might well be dominating the headlines on the behalf of the Norwegians. But Nusa is not far behind him, having continued his rapid rise with some energetic performances and fearless assaults on full backs.

Nusa looks capable of creating danger whenever he gets the ball, suggesting he will be a pivotal part of his international side for years to come.

He also looks capable of leaving Leipzig behind in search of a much bigger stage - and several English clubs could well be prepared to give it to him.

‌

Sports.content:
Rio Ferdinand sends Aurelien Tchouameni Man Utd transfer plea - ‘we’ve had a few conversations'

Aurelien Tchouameni has been a long-term target for Manchester United and Rio Ferdinand has weighed in on the potential transfer

View 2 Images Aurelien Tchouameni has been handed a transfer caution (Image: Visionhaus/Getty Images)

Rio Ferdinand has urged Aurelien Tchouameni to make Manchester United his next destination, insisting there is "only one club" for the Real Madrid midfielder. The French star has long been on the radar of Michael Carrick's side, with a separate transfer development potentially opening the door for a deal.

‌



Madrid's reported interest in Chelsea's Enzo Fernandes could work in United's favour, with The Athletic suggesting it may create an opportunity for them to land Tchouameni's signature. However, the France international's hefty £210,000-a-week wages in Spain could prove a significant stumbling block.

‌



Despite this, Ferdinand is insistent that United must not allow the midfielder to slip from their grasp should he become available. Speaking on Rio Presents, the former England defender said: "If Tchouameni has half a sniff of getting out of that club, Man United have to be the first team at their door knocking and make sure he can't even talk to anybody else.

‌



"Get him signed, sealed, delivered. Tchouameni? I know we've had a few conversations in private but man, I know you watch the show, I'm looking down the lens right now at you. Behind these shades, there is only one club for you man.

"If you are looking to leave Real Madrid, we are the club , Man United are the club. If you want to make it happen, make the call, that's what I'd do."

‌



Co-host Joel Beya cheekily added: "If not, you can always come to Arsenal. Just asking," to which Ferdinand replied: "You don't want to go to Arsenal, you don't need them. He don't want to go to you lot."

Reports from SportItalia suggest that Madrid are willing to allow the 26 year old to depart, though he is determined to remain with the La Liga heavyweights. Tchouameni could follow the path of former team-mate Casemiro, who signed for United and proceeded to claim two domestic trophies during his spell.

View 2 Images The Real Madrid star has caught the eye of United (Image: Jewel SAMAD / AFP via Getty Images)

‌



However, Tchouameni isn't the sole midfielder United are monitoring this summer. Mateus Fernandes has surfaced as a target once more for the club, with the player appearing set to exit West Ham this summer.

Atalanta's Ederson virtually confirmed his switch to Old Trafford was finalised after declaring that it is "almost all sorted."

United reached an agreement earlier this month to bring in the midfielder for an initial £35million plus £3.8m in performance-related bonuses.

Sports.title: Newcastle to rival Man Utd for £73m World Cup star as midfield replacement
Sports.content:
Newcastle to rival Man Utd for £73m World Cup star as midfield replacement

Newcastle could be forced into the transfer market for a new midfielder, with Bruno Guimaraes and Sandro Tonali emerging as targets for Arsenal and Tottenham respectively

View 2 Images Michael Carrick and Eddie Howe have the same target (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

Newcastle have shortlisted Manchester United target Felix Nmecha ahead of a potential midfield rebuild. The Magpies face losing both Bruno Guimaraes and Sandro Tonali this summer to Premier League rivals.

‌



Tottenham have reportedly agreed personal terms with Tonali while Arsenal have seen a bid for Guimaraes rejected. Newcastle are therefore making contingency plans and could steal a march on United.

‌



Nmecha, 25, is one of the midfielders under consideration at St James' Park, the Mail report. It's added that the German has been on Eddie Howe's radar for several years.

‌



Currently at the World Cup with Germany, Nmecha has started all three of their group stage matches, returning one goal and one assist. He has a £73.5million release clause in his contract with Borussia Dortmund, who signed him from fellow Bundesliga club Wolfsburg in 2023.

Get the latest World Cup 2026 news in your inbox with our Make Football Great Again newsletter

Manuel Ugarte inconsolable as Man Utd star stretchered off after freak World Cup injury READ MORE :

Prior to that, Nmecha spent 14 years on the books of Manchester City, making three first-team appearances under Pep Guardiola. His elder brother, Lukas, was also at City as a youngster and now plays for Leeds.

‌



Nmecha is under contract at Dortmund until 2030, having signed a new long-term deal back in March before he helped Niko Kovac's side finish second and secure Champions League football. But that hasn't prevented speculation over his future, especially after Germany topped their World Cup group and booked a round-of-32 clash with Paraguay.

A box-to-box midfielder, he enjoys getting forward and firing off shots, scoring six goals while registering three assists last season. But his 6ft 3in frame allows him to win aerial duels and break up play.

Should Felix Nmecha join Newcastle or Manchester United? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Felix Nmecha has started every game for Germany (Image: Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images)

Having moved to Manchester as a child, he'd likely have no problem settling back into English life. Raised by a Nigerian father and a German mother, he's embraced each of the cultures that he's experienced.

"With Nigeria a lot of the culture is food, happiness, even just the business mindset, being disciplined," Nmecha told SW magazine. "Then the German side is also very disciplined and has good values and morals.

Article continues below

"And then the England side, I think a lot of English people are very open when it comes to conversations, having a laugh and hard working as well."
